published_source: Figure 4 (category sweet bakery (file: 'fresh sweet bakery, packaged sweet bakery, and frozen bakery')); the text reports -8.8%, coef = implied log points ln(1 + -8.8%); SE only readable from the figure.
replication_status: failed (synthetic data by design; see notes)
notes: Category-level STATIC TWFE, outcome ln(1 + monthly household spending on sweet bakery (file: 'fresh sweet bakery, packaged sweet bakery, and frozen bakery')). The authors' Figure 4 code is already static: feols(lnspend_cat ~ i(glp1use) | user_id + month_num, cluster user_id) on regdata_not0_6m (matched households; adopters restricted to relative months -6..6 excluding month 0; controls all 27 months) merged with the CategoryAggregation file summed to user-month; glp1use = 1 while on GLP-1, 0 before, NA after discontinuation (dropped). Here the NA (switched-off) rows are dropped explicitly and g_idx = adoption month index. Category files cover all 22,691 households x 33 months (Jan 2022-Sep 2024) including zero-spend months, so the merge keeps every regression row (100,472 before dropping switched-off rows; 98,909 after). Matched sample = 2,602 adopters + 2,602 never-adopters (MatchIt 1:1 nearest-neighbour logit, no replacement, Jul-Dec 2022 covariates; match.csv re-created in the work dir because the package does not ship it). SYNTHETIC DATA: the Dataverse package (doi:10.7910/DVN/SVWBNT) ships only Data_clean_synth; spending profiles are reshuffled across households and rescaled, so by design no coefficient reproduces (README Section 4). Adoption timing, use duration, discontinuation and stated reason are preserved; income is not.
